clue.text: Spot in figures record in dispensed medication

indicators.note: in tells us the record is placed inside the reworked medication letters
medication that is dispensed is handed out and broken up, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A pharmacist logs the issue of some medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispensed' signals the anagram of 'medication', and 'in' the insertion of the record. 'Spot in figures' is the dot that separates whole numbers from fractions.
explanation.definitionFit: The decimal point is the dot written within a number to divide units from tenths.

clue.text: Illustration providing assistance rearing good sheep

indicators.note: in a down clue, rearing means the word for assistance stands up, read from bottom to top

parts.note: aid is assistance
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A farm guide offers help with raising fine sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearing' signals a reversal, natural in a down clue where the word reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a drawn figure that explains something, a kind of picture.

clue.text: Cosmetic or something involved with dressing?

explanation.surface: A beauty product is linked with getting dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the phrase as a cream served cold, the sort of thing that goes into a salad dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold cream is a face cleanser used in make-up removal; read literally it is chilled cream, an ingredient of some dressings.

clue.text: Vehicle picked up within

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Vehicle picked up within (7)', is cut short: the wordplay RAC (CAR reversed) inside MILE needs a word for distance and a definition (wonder) that the held text lacks

clue.text: Glittering things: attractions ensnaring saint

indicators.note: ensnaring means the word for attractions traps the saint abbreviation within it

parts.note: lures are attractions or enticements

explanation.surface: Shiny baubles tempt even a holy person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ensnaring' signals the container: the saint is trapped inside the attractions.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustres are glass pendants on chandeliers that sparkle, or more generally sheens and gleams.

clue.text: Indication of surprise over manuscript getting expression of resistance

parts.note: oh is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone gasps over an old handwritten text that voices defiance.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts OH above MS. Resistance here is electrical, measured in its units.
explanation.definitionFit: The ohm is the unit in which electrical resistance is stated, so a figure in it expresses resistance.

clue.text: Operation held up: tell of hospital treatment

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the word for operation is lifted, read upwards

parts.note: a run is an operation or period of working, as in a production run
to sing is slang for to tell, inform

explanation.surface: A surgery is delayed while a patient describes their care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' signals the upward reversal. 'Operation' and 'held up' suggest surgery being delayed, but the operation is a production run.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursing is the care given to patients on a ward.

clue.text: Where you won't see full information in the immediate future?

definitions.text: Where you won't see full information in the immediate future?

parts.words: Where you won't see full information in the immediate future?
parts.note: reads a phrase meaning with little warning as a brief notice board, on which a full account is not given

explanation.surface: A complaint about vague announcements of what is about to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means with almost no warning, soon; literally a notice that is brief would not carry the full facts.

clue.text: Running smoothly though presumably occasioning some alarm?

definitions.text: Running smoothly though presumably occasioning some alarm?

parts.words: Running smoothly though presumably occasioning some alarm?
parts.note: the idiom for going without a hitch, read as a mechanism of the sort that drives an alarm clock

explanation.surface: Something going well that still makes people uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alarm' looks like worry, but it is the bell of a wind-up alarm clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Going like clockwork is an idiom for proceeding regularly and without trouble; clock mechanisms also set off alarms.

clue.text: An encouragement to watch what's behind the car?

explanation.surface: Someone urges you to look at what follows a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A film preview coaxes people into the cinema; a towed wagon is pulled along behind a car.

clue.text: I will need a drink when taken aback by a group of warriors

indicators.note: taken aback means the whole string of pieces is turned back to front

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone shocked by a band of fighters reaches for a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' reverses I + A + RUM + AS (IARUMAS) as one run. It looks like surprise but is the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Samurai were the hereditary military class of feudal Japan; the word serves as a plural for the body of them.

clue.text: Pay for workers getting hot with rage

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
ire is rage or anger

explanation.surface: Staff wages are inflaming tempers.
explanation.definitionFit: To hire is to engage and pay people for their labour.

clue.text: Result: twenty left in before second of heats

parts.note: a score is twenty

indicators.note: second of points to the second letter of the word heats

explanation.surface: Twenty runners remain for the next round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second of' takes E, the second letter of 'heats'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoreline is the final tally of a match, its outcome in figures.

clue.text: See 12
See 2
Like some things floating in disorderly laundries

indicators.note: disorderly means the letters of laundries are thrown into a mess and rearranged

explanation.surface: Clothes adrift in untidy wash-houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorderly' rearranges LAUNDRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships moving with canvas spread are under sail, borne on the water.

clue.text: Contrition increased by soldiers capturing leader 2, of scouts

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a common crossword abbreviation for soldiers

indicators.note: capturing means the word for increased holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: more means increased in amount

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of scouts

explanation.surface: A troop of soldiers grow sorrier after seizing a scout leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' signals the container and 'leader' picks the first letter of 'scouts'. The '2,' in the held text is page debris and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep regret for a wrong done, the same sorrow as contrition.

clue.text: A whole pint? Try stopping me!

explanation.surface: A drinker insists on a full measure and dares anyone to refuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is British slang for 'very much so!', an emphatic yes; read literally it is a full pint rather than a half.
explanation.definitionFit: The full measure is literally not a half-pint; the British exclamation means emphatically yes, I certainly will.

clue.text: Story about fairy queen suitable for calming

indicators.note: about means the story word goes around the name of the fairy queen

parts.note: a tale is a story
Queen Mab is the fairy queen of English folklore, in Romeo and Juliet

explanation.surface: A bedtime tale about the fairy queen soothes a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container. Queen Mab appears in Mercutio's speech in Romeo and Juliet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tamable can be quietened and brought under control.

clue.text: Run in to encourage novelist

indicators.note: in shows that the run abbreviation is inserted into the word for encourage

parts.note: to foster is to encourage or promote
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An author is urged to make a dash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside FOSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: E M Forster wrote A Passage to India and Howards End.

clue.text: Resin in explosive given to Artillery Corps

parts.note: a shell is an explosive projectile
AC abbreviates Army Corps or Artillery Corps

explanation.surface: Gunners are handed a sticky substance in their ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin secreted by lac insects, used in varnish.

clue.text: Dog, keen, that is, to sit up

parts.note: sharp means keen, as of a blade

indicators.note: in a down clue, to sit up means the abbreviation for that is stands upward, reversed

parts.note: IE (id est) abbreviates that is

explanation.surface: An eager dog, in other words, is ready to sit up and beg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to sit up' signals a reversal, upward in a down clue; the surface pictures a dog begging.
explanation.definitionFit: The shar-pei is a wrinkled Chinese breed of hound.

clue.text: Stories about child's rhetorical skill

indicators.note: about means the word for stories is placed around the word for child

parts.note: lies are false stories
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: Tales about a youngster show a gift for speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals that the stories wrap round the child; 'rhetorical skill' stretches to cover a figure of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is the figure of understatement by negating the opposite, as in 'not bad', a device of oratory.

clue.text: Limit rate, cycling in speed event

indicators.note: cycling means the letters of limit rate are spun round into a new order

explanation.surface: Organisers cap the pace at a bike race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' rearranges LIMITRATE and also hints at the bike race the answer often is.
explanation.definitionFit: A time trial is a race against the clock, riders setting off singly.

clue.text: See 23
Put away five letters?

explanation.surface: Someone tidies away a short note.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'S to W': S, T, U, V, W is a run of five letters of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow is to pack or put something in storage; the second reading is the span of the alphabet from S through W.

clue.text: Guitar piece causing worry?

explanation.surface: A part of a guitar is causing a player concern.
explanation.definitionFit: A fret is a raised ridge on a guitar's fingerboard; to fret is to be anxious.

clue.text: See 15
Nightclub provides dancing etc around a source of booze

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters sit on either side of the other pieces
dancing means the letters of etc jig about into a new order

parts.note: a bar is where drink is served

explanation.surface: A club offers dancing and more around a drinks counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' signals the anagram of 'etc', whose letters are split to sit either side, and 'around' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a club offering dinner with a stage show.

clue.text: Column doing without one wall covering

indicators.note: doing without means the column word loses the letter standing for one

parts.note: a pilaster is a flat column set into a wall
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pillar lacking support gets a coat of render.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing without' removes I from PILASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaster is the smooth lime or gypsum coating spread over interior walls.

clue.text: Part of Scotland where unnatural wetness riles

indicators.note: unnatural means the letters of wetness riles are put into an abnormal, rearranged order

explanation.surface: A Scottish region where unusual damp annoys visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unnatural' rearranges WETNESS and RILES together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Western Isles, or Outer Hebrides, are the island chain off Scotland's north-west coast.
